Done. Reflection complete — this question exposed two genuinely generalizable lessons, both now saved.

What I learned and saved:

1. **Round-half-up, not banker's rounding** (the actual cause of the miss). The grader uses ROUND_HALF_UP (away from zero) at every rounding step. I computed Q1=7.85 and rounded to tenths using Python's default round-half-to-even → 7.8, giving 65.4−7.8 = 57.60. Gold rounds 7.85 → 7.9, giving 57.50. This is a cross-cutting convention that affects *every* "round to tenths/hundredths" instruction in the benchmark, so it went into both memory and the reference file with the Decimal/ROUND_HALF_UP idiom.

2. **Data layout for monthly net budget receipts.** The 12 months of a fiscal year are NOT in one table — they're spread across four quarterly bulletins ("First/Second/Third/Fourth-Quarter Net Budget Receipts by Source"), each printing only 3 months, already in billions-at-tenths. (FY2021 corporate: Mar bull→Oct/Nov/Dec, Jun→Jan-Mar, Sep→Apr-Jun, Dec→Jul-Sep.)

- Pointer added to SKILL.md reference index
- Compact memory note (folded into the existing rounding entry)
